facts.statement: Phyllodontosuchus is a genus of sphenosuchian, which is a type of basal crocodylomorph.
facts.quote: Phyllodontosuchus (Ancient Greek, meaning "leaf tooth crocodile", in reference to the shape of the middle and posterior teeth) is a genus of sphenosuchian, a type of basal crocodylomorph

facts.statement: The animal is known from a skull and jaws found in Lower Jurassic rocks in Yunnan, China.
facts.quote: It is known from a skull and jaws from Lower Jurassic rocks of Yunnan, China

facts.statement: Some of its teeth were leaf-shaped, resembling those of certain herbivorous dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Phyllodontosuchus is unusual because some of its teeth were leaf-shaped, like those of some herbivorous dinosaurs

facts.statement: The holotype specimen is only 71.4 mm long and is imperfectly preserved.
facts.quote: BVP568-L12 is only 71.4 mm long and imperfectly preserved

facts.statement: The genus was named in 2000 by Jerald Harris and colleagues.
facts.quote: Phyllodontosuchus was named in 2000 by Jerald Harris and colleagues

facts.statement: The type species is P. lufengensis, named after the Lufeng Formation.
facts.quote: The type species is P. lufengensis, in reference to the Lufeng Formation

facts.statement: The first five or six teeth were pointed, conical, and curved backward.
facts.quote: The first five or six were pointed, conical, and curved backward

facts.statement: The animal lived during the Sinemurian age, between 199.5 and 192.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Sinemurian to Sinemurian (199.5 to 192.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: It is classified in the class Reptilia.
